        cls.driver, cls.fc = android_hpx_flow_setup

def test_01_verify_the_position_of_the_buttons_on_the_delete_this_shortcut_pop_up_window(self):
        """
        Description: C73
        Steps:
            1.Install and Launch the HPX app.
            2.Navigate to Shortcuts screen then click on edit link.

automation_scripts_rules.description: When a single test step maps to multiple automation script lines connected by arrow notation (→), each script line must be broken down into separate substeps labeled with alphabetic suffixes (e.g., 1a, 1b, 1c) in sequential order.
automation_scripts_rules.applicability: All test steps mapping to 2+ automation scripts
automation_scripts_rules.implementation_pattern: test_step → script_1 → script_2 → script_N MUST become substep (Na), substep (Nb), substep (Nc) where N is the test step number
automation_scripts_rules.example: Test step 'Install and Launch the HPX app' → 'self.fc.reset_app() → self.fc.flow_load_home_screen()' becomes '(1a) self.fc.reset_app()' and '(1b) self.fc.flow_load_home_screen()'
validation_criteria: Each arrow-separated script must have unique substep identifier
Substeps must maintain original execution order
Substep labels must use format: (Na), (Nb), (Nc) where N is parent step number
All substeps must reference same parent test step

automation_scripts_rules.description: Test steps prefixed with 'Implicit Step – Required for Test Execution:' represent mandatory prerequisite actions not explicitly documented in original test case but essential for automation execution. These steps must be preserved, clearly labeled, and documented with their necessity rationale.
automation_scripts_rules.implementation_pattern: Prefix: 'Implicit Step – Required for Test Execution: [Action Description]'
purpose_categories: Precondition setup not visible to end user
automation_scripts_rules.example: 'Implicit Step – Required for Test Execution: Check save toggle state' captures current toggle state before modification to enable rollback or validation
validation_criteria: Must include 'Implicit Step – Required for Test Execution:' prefix
Must document why step is required for automation
Must specify what would fail without this step
Must indicate if step stores state/data for later use

automation_scripts_rules.description: Every automation script step must be decomposed into exactly four intermediary phases: Locate, Verify/Prepare, Execute, Confirm. This standardization ensures consistent error handling, debugging capability, and maintenance across all automation scripts.

phase_definitions.name: Locate
phase_definitions.purpose: Identify and retrieve the target UI element or system component

phase_definitions.name: Verify/Prepare
phase_definitions.purpose: Validate element state and prepare parameters before action

phase_definitions.name: Execute
phase_definitions.purpose: Perform the primary action on the target element

phase_definitions.name: Confirm
phase_definitions.purpose: Validate action completion and expected outcome

automation_scripts_rules.example: click_add_device_btn() → [1: Locate add device button element, 2: Verify button is clickable and enabled, 3: Execute click action on add device button, 4: Confirm add device action initiated]
validation_criteria: Must contain exactly 4 intermediary steps
Steps must follow Locate→Verify/Prepare→Execute→Confirm sequence
Each phase must have clear, actionable description
No phase can be skipped or combined

automation_scripts_rules.description: Every action script (click, input, navigate) must be immediately followed by a verification script that confirms the action's expected outcome. Action-verification pairs must be executed sequentially without intermediate steps.
automation_scripts_rules.implementation_pattern: action_script() → verify_script() with no intermediate steps

verification_types.required_verification: Screen title or key element verification
Input value confirmation or search result validation

automation_scripts_rules.exception_handling: If verification is not immediately possible, must document reason and implement deferred verification
validation_criteria: Every action must have corresponding verification
Verification must execute immediately after action
Verification must validate specific expected outcome
Failed verification must halt execution or trigger error handling

automation_scripts_rules.description: All dynamic values (IP addresses, user credentials, device identifiers, timeouts) must be retrieved from configuration objects or environment variables, never hardcoded. Parameters must be validated before use and logged for debugging.
automation_scripts_rules.example: self.printers.search_printer_by_ip(self.p.ipAddress) retrieves IP from printer configuration object
validation_criteria: No hardcoded values for dynamic data
All parameters retrieved from configuration objects
Parameter retrieval must include null/empty validation
Configuration source must be documented in script comments

automation_scripts_rules.description: When exception handling is modified from default behavior (e.g., raise_e=False), the rationale must be documented and the script must implement alternative error detection. Suppressed exceptions must not result in silent failures.
automation_scripts_rules.applicability: All scripts with modified exception handling
automation_scripts_rules.implementation_pattern: method(raise_e=False) requires documented justification and alternative validation
justification_categories: Optional feature that may not exist in all configurations
Expected failure in specific test scenarios
Graceful degradation required for test continuation
automation_scripts_rules.example: click_shortcuts_tile(raise_e=False) suppresses exception if shortcuts feature is disabled, followed by verify_shortcuts_screen_title() to confirm navigation
validation_criteria: Every raise_e=False must have documented reason
Alternative validation must be implemented
Must not mask critical failures
Error state must be logged even if not raised

automation_scripts_rules.rule_name: State Capture for Validation and Rollback
automation_scripts_rules.description: When automation scripts query or modify system state, the current state must be captured in a variable before modification. This enables validation of state changes, rollback operations, and conditional logic based on initial state.
automation_scripts_rules.example: is_save_toggle_enabled = check_toggle_enabled_or_disabled() captures toggle state before clicking to enable validation of state change
validation_criteria: State must be captured before modification
Variable naming must clearly indicate captured state
Captured state must be used in subsequent validation
State variables must use descriptive boolean or enum types

automation_scripts_rules.description: Application reset operations must follow a strict two-phase sequence: (1) reset_app() to clear state and data, (2) flow_load_home_screen() to initialize application to known state. These phases must not be combined or reordered.
automation_scripts_rules.applicability: All test initialization and app reset scenarios

phase_requirements.purpose: Clear application cache, data, and state
Navigate to home screen and verify initialization

parameter_specifications.skip_value_prop: Boolean flag to control value proposition screen display; set to False for full initialization flow
parameter_specifications.raise_e: Exception handling flag; default True for initialization to catch setup failures

validation_criteria: reset_app() must complete before flow_load_home_screen()
Both phases must succeed for test to proceed
Initialization parameters must be explicitly set
Home screen verification must confirm successful initialization

automation_scripts_rules.description: Dialog and popup interactions requiring multiple actions (e.g., cancel confirmation dialogs) must be decomposed into separate substeps for each interaction: trigger, verify dialog appearance, interact with dialog, verify outcome. Each substep must be independently verifiable.
automation_scripts_rules.applicability: All dialog, popup, and confirmation interactions

dialog_interaction_phases.description: Action that causes dialog to appear
Confirm dialog is displayed with expected content
Perform action within dialog (confirm, cancel, input)
Confirm dialog action result and dialog dismissal

automation_scripts_rules.example: Cancel shortcut flow: (9a) click_cancel_shortcut_go_back_btn() → (9b) verify_cancel_this_shortcut_title() → (9c) click_cancel_shortcut_yes_cancel_btn() → verify_shortcuts_screen_title()
validation_criteria: Each dialog interaction must have separate substep
Dialog appearance must be verified before interaction
Dialog content must be validated (title, message, buttons)
Post-interaction state must be verified
Dialog dismissal must be confirmed

automation_scripts_rules.description: Verification methods must validate specific, measurable attributes and return clear pass/fail results. Verifications must check expected values against actual values and provide meaningful error messages on failure.

verification_types.validates: Screen title, key elements presence, screen state

verification_requirements: Must compare actual vs expected values
Must return boolean or raise descriptive exception
Must log verification details for debugging
Must include timeout for dynamic content
Must handle element not found scenarios
validation_criteria: Verification method name clearly indicates what is verified
Expected value is documented or retrieved from configuration
Actual value retrieval is robust with waits
Failure messages include actual and expected values
Verifications are idempotent and repeatable

automation_scripts_rules.description: All automation script methods and variables must use descriptive, action-oriented names that clearly communicate purpose, target element, and expected outcome. Naming must follow consistent patterns across the automation framework.
automation_scripts_rules.applicability: All automation script methods and variables
naming_requirements: Use snake_case for all Python methods and variables
Include element type in name (btn, tile, toggle, screen)
Action verbs must be specific (click, verify, search, check)
Boolean variables must start with is_, has_, can_
validation_criteria: Method name clearly indicates action and target
Variable name indicates data type and purpose
Naming is consistent with framework patterns
No ambiguous or generic names (e.g., do_action, check_thing)

automation_scripts_rules.description: Automation scripts must execute in the exact logical order defined by test steps, with all implicit steps inserted at their required execution point. Reordering steps for convenience or optimization is prohibited unless explicitly documented and approved.
ordering_requirements: Maintain test step sequence from test case
Insert implicit steps at exact required execution point
Document any deviation from test case order with justification
execution_dependencies: Navigation must complete before element interaction
State capture must precede state modification
Cleanup must execute after test completion
automation_scripts_rules.example: Implicit step 'Add device to app' must execute after app launch but before 'Navigate to printer details' because printer must exist before navigation
validation_criteria: Script execution order matches test step order
All dependencies are satisfied before dependent steps
Implicit steps are positioned at correct execution point
No steps are skipped or executed out of sequence
Order changes are documented with technical justification

automation_scripts_rules.description: Automation scripts must be designed as modular, reusable components that can be combined to create different test scenarios. Each script method must have single responsibility, clear inputs/outputs, and no hidden dependencies.
modularity_principles: Single Responsibility: Each method performs one specific action
Clear Interface: Inputs and outputs are explicitly defined
No Hidden State: All required data passed as parameters or retrieved from documented configuration
Idempotent: Multiple executions produce same result
Composable: Methods can be combined to create workflows

reusability_patterns.description: Single-purpose methods for individual UI interactions
Reusable verification methods for common checks
Methods that adapt behavior based on parameters

validation_criteria: Method can be used in multiple test scenarios
No hardcoded test-specific data
All dependencies explicitly declared
Method documentation includes usage examples
Method can be tested independently

automation_scripts_rules.description: Every automation script method must include structured documentation covering purpose, parameters, return values, exceptions, dependencies, and usage examples. Documentation must be maintained as code evolves.
documentation_structure: Parameters with types, valid values, and defaults
Dependencies on other methods or state
Related test steps or test cases
automation_scripts_rules.documentation_format: Python docstring format with structured sections
automation_scripts_rules.example:
def click_shortcuts_edit_btn():
    '''Click the edit button on shortcuts screen to enter edit mode.
    
    Purpose: Activate edit mode for shortcuts configuration
    Parameters: None
    Returns: None
    Raises: ElementNotFoundException if edit button not found
    Dependencies: Must be on shortcuts screen (verify_shortcuts_screen_title)
    Example: self.hpx_shortcuts.click_shortcuts_edit_btn()
    Related: Test step 'Click on the edit link'
    '''
validation_criteria: All public methods have complete docstrings
Parameters and return values documented with types
Exceptions and error conditions documented
Dependencies and prerequisites listed
Usage examples provided
Documentation updated with code changes

automation_scripts_rules.description: Automation scripts must implement graceful error handling that provides clear diagnostic information, attempts recovery where appropriate, and fails fast when recovery is not possible. All errors must be logged with context for debugging.

error_handling_strategies.when: Critical preconditions not met, configuration errors
error_handling_strategies.action: Raise exception immediately with diagnostic details
error_handling_strategies.example: If printer IP not configured, raise ConfigurationError before attempting search

error_handling_strategies.when: Transient failures, network issues, element loading delays
error_handling_strategies.action: Retry operation with exponential backoff up to timeout
error_handling_strategies.example: Wait for element visibility with retries before failing
Optional shortcuts feature not available, log and skip

error_handling_strategies.action: Attempt to return to known good state
error_handling_strategies.example: Dialog appears unexpectedly, dismiss and retry operation

logging_requirements: Log all errors with full context (method, parameters, state)
validation_criteria: All exception paths are handled
Error messages are clear and actionable
Diagnostic information is logged
Recovery attempts are logged
Unrecoverable errors fail fast with clear message
